issues.legal_issue: Retrospective application of a requirement that transfers of evacuee property be confirmed does not, in the circumstances, deprive the transferee of property or violate a fundamental right.
material_facts: The purchaser completed a genuine transfer of evacuee agricultural property before the relevant legislation and its amendment introduced a confirmation requirement.
The purchaser paid most of the consideration and received possession, and the transfer was later recorded by the revenue authorities.
The confirmation requirement was made retrospective, and the authority refused to confirm the transfer under a policy against confirming transactions involving agricultural property.
issues.conclusion: The retrospective confirmation requirement was a restriction on the transfer of property, not a deprivation of property. In the circumstances, the requirement was reasonable and its retrospective operation did not violate the purchaser’s fundamental rights.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5-A of the East Punjab Evacuees’ (Administration of Property) Act, 1947, as inserted by amendment, made specified transfers ineffective to confer rights or remedies unless confirmed. The Court treated the requirement, in substance, as a restriction on transfers within Article 19 rather than a deprivation within Article 31. Given the purpose of evacuee-property legislation and the abnormal conditions surrounding evacuee property, the confirmation requirement was reasonable; giving it retrospective effect did not convert that restriction into a deprivation. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: article_32_fundamental_right_petition and transfer_involved_evacuee_property and transfer_predated_confirmation_rule and confirmation_rule_applied_retroactively and confirmation_was_refused and law_addressed_abnormal_evacuee_property_conditions

predicates.article_32_fundamental_right_petition: The proceeding is a petition seeking relief for an alleged violation of a fundamental right.
predicates.transfer_involved_evacuee_property: A person acquired property belonging to someone who had become an evacuee.
predicates.transfer_predated_confirmation_rule: The transfer was completed before a rule requiring confirmation of such transfers took effect.
predicates.confirmation_rule_applied_retroactively: The confirmation requirement was applied to a transfer completed before the requirement took effect.
predicates.confirmation_was_refused: The authority declined to confirm the transfer.
predicates.law_addressed_abnormal_evacuee_property_: The law addressed the exceptional conditions affecting property associated with evacuees.

issues.definition: When a fundamental-rights petition concerns a completed transfer of evacuee property that is later subjected to a retrospective confirmation requirement, and confirmation is refused under a law addressing exceptional evacuee-property conditions, the requirement is treated as a reasonable restriction rather than a property deprivation.

issues.legal_issue: An allegation that an authority relied on an improper administrative circular, without raising a fundamental-rights violation, does not establish a basis for relief under Article 32.
material_facts: The authority refused confirmation while acting on an administrative circular stating a policy against confirming transactions involving agricultural property.
The purchaser argued that the circular was not relevant material under the governing provision and that relying on it was illegal.
The Court assumed that the argument might be correct but held that this would not, by itself, raise a question of violation of a fundamental right.
issues.conclusion: Even if reliance on the circular was legally erroneous, the complaint did not establish a fundamental-rights violation; the Article 32 petition was misconceived on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Article 32 provides a remedy for enforcement of fundamental rights. An alleged error in an authority’s application of the governing law, without a resulting fundamental-rights violation, does not by itself support relief under Article 32. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.article_32_fundamental_right_petition: The proceeding is a petition seeking relief for an alleged violation of a fundamental right.
predicates.decision_relied_on_administrative_circul: The authority based its decision on an administrative circular.
predicates.claim_concerns_only_legality_under_gover: The complaint is that the authority acted unlawfully under the governing law, rather than that its action violated a fundamental right.
predicates.no_fundamental_right_violation_is_assert: The petitioner identifies no fundamental-rights violation arising from the alleged legal error.

issues.definition: When a fundamental-rights petition challenges an authority’s reliance on a circular only as an error under the governing law and identifies no fundamental-rights violation, relief under that petition is unavailable for the error.
